ops.entry: WHEN removing or redirecting under bash-write-guard DO use a literal absolute target path — an rm or redirect whose target contains a shell variable is blocked even under /tmp; pipe to grep inside mutant loops, and drive scratch-tree setup and cleanup from a python script (shutil).
ops.why: Observed this feature: rm with a variable target is blocked too, not only redirects; the python driver was the working route. Extends G-13 at equal scope.

ops.entry: WHEN citing a test-check-plan-routes.py CANONICAL_READER_CASES case as evidence DO cite the CI step `check-plan-routes.py --canonical-reader-audit` instead — those cases run only under `--canonical-reader-self-test`, which neither run-unit-tests.py nor CI invokes, so they cannot redden.
ops.why: A named SC test in that registry could never redden through a cycle; re-verified at main 86ce6ba: only the test file itself references the self-test flag, while .github/workflows/tests.yml:243 runs the audit.

originals.original: WHEN redirecting output under bash-write-guard DO use a literal absolute target path — a redirect whose target contains a shell variable (e.g. `> mut-$m.txt`) is blocked even under /tmp; pipe to grep inside mutant loops instead.

ops.entry: WHEN asserting a token in output, present or absent, DO bind it to the specific field or structured record and confirm no fixture-supplied value (ids, names, paths) echoed there already contains it — a bare substring check passes vacuously on unrelated or self-supplied text.
ops.why: A fixture id containing the asserted marker made a token clause vacuous; a reason-dropping mutant stayed green a full cycle. Sharpens P-02's substring-vacuity rule to cover self-supplied text, same length.

ops.entry: WHEN judging whether a mutation proof discriminates DO compare against a control differing in one factor — the mutant's effect neutered while its reached-marker fires, or, after a test-only fix, the pre-fix tests run on the same mutant; only a red the control lacks proves discrimination.
ops.why: Running pre-fix tests against the same mutant (green) beside the fixed tests (red) is what proved a test repair closed a vacuity finding; generalizes P-09's neutered-effect arm into one control-arm rule instead of adding to a full section.

ops.entry: WHEN crediting a test as a required kind's evidence DO confirm that kind's cmd actually executes it — the file on the runner's explicit list and the case reachable without a flag or env the runner never passes; a glob match or flag-gated registry reports satisfied while never running.
ops.why: A named SC case was registered only under a self-test flag no runner invokes, so it could never redden; same failure class as P-14's glob-without-list-membership, so P-14 is broadened rather than a new entry added to a full section.

originals.original: WHEN scoping a negative assertion (e.g. "X was not closed") DO confirm it filters a structured call log to the specific operation, not a stdout substring check — a substring check can pass vacuously if unrelated output happens to contain the same text.

WHEN judging whether a mutation-proof arm is vacuous DO neuter its specific effect while keeping the 'reached' marker firing — if the case stays green despite the marker firing, the arm proves only that the mutant installed, not that its effect discriminates the case.

WHEN a required kind's `detect` glob matches a changed file DO also confirm that kind's `cmd` actually runs the file, via an explicit script list — a glob match without list membership means the kind reports satisfied while the binding suite never executes.
